scope: Small independent near-ground detail helper for the existing GSU Link forecourt

verifiedVisibleFeatures: Low pale concrete slab benches on short independent feet along the planted forecourt edge.
Shallow planted border below ground-floor windows, containing low shrubs.
Mature deciduous courtyard tree with a dark metal root grate, surrounded by the brick/stone pavement.
source.boundary: The photograph verifies furniture and planting types, not the exact coordinates or tree species. In particular the small eastern bench position is an authored fitting of that typology, not a surveyed object.

implementation.frame: Existing BU_SERT_FRAME / buSertPoint, x east, z south, coordinates in metres
implementation.benches: Three low slab seats, each with two separate feet and an actual open underside; seat height 0.44m above its highest adjacent paving, not terrain-warped slabs.
implementation.treePit: One 1.12m radius soil patch with two thin iron rings and 24 open radial bars. Soil and rings are just above existing paving; no blanket ground replacement.
implementation.planting: Nine low shrubs represented by separate shaped leaves in two material batches. Desktop 42 leaves each, phone 16 each. No opaque hedge boxes.
implementation.collision: Low concrete, soil and grate are returned as actual support geometry; concrete is also wall geometry. No inflated invisible wall. The caller generates the tree/trunk collision at the same tree record.
implementation.ground: All existing court paving, DEM, door sill and routes are unchanged. Shallow planted borders follow the existing terrain, bench feet reach local paving.

estimatesAndLimits: All furniture and tree positions, sections, mature tree size and shrub habit are photograph-based authored approximations, not a field survey.
Only one clearly supported courtyard tree is added; no speculative symmetric pair or new railings.
Tree foliage is created by the parent scene from the returned tree record. Its geometry is additional to the helper counts.
The small helper does not reconstruct all GSU/Mugar landscape or change the building facade.

validation.result: 17 focused tests and TypeScript build passed before scene integration
checks: Every inspected new geometry triangle vertex lies outside actual existing Sert building collision.
6.9m-wide central corridor remains supported with no new furniture ground/wall intersections; entire arrival-to-door approach retained.
Visible seats match downward support rays; horizontal rays verify a real gap below the slab and solid feet.
Desktop/mobile furniture and support vertex arrays, tree records and root elevations match exactly.
Finite geometry, bounded batches/triangles and idempotent disposal.
validation.visualQA: Runtime screenshots remain the parent integration task; unit tests do not assert visual realism.
